summary: Aluwind has scaled its façade business, but the investment case is not yet a cash-compounding story. FY26 revenue reached ₹138.5649 crore and group PAT ₹10.4455 crore, while operating cash flow was negative ₹16.3335 crore. Restricted deposits leave only ₹0.2893 crore of freely available March cash against ₹41.3195 crore of debt. The proposed ₹20 crore expansion adds capacity and funding risk simultaneously. Watchlist only, with weak implementation liquidity and substantial downside; this is not a trade instruction.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Reviewed as of 20 October 2026. Legal issuer is Aluwind Infra-Tech Limited, formerly Aluwind Architectural Limited, renamed 16 April 2025; ISIN INE0 STM01017, NSE Emerge symbol ALUWIND, listed 9 April 2024. The quote is the 19 October close, not a live executable price. FY26 includes newly formed Aluwind Clean-Tech; earlier history is the parent, which remains overwhelmingly dominant. Historical statements, original comparatives, prospectus, subsequent announcements and dated market files support Medium evidence confidence. All four gates are Conditional: no proved integrity failure, usable audited aggregate financial inputs, explicit but unapproved future financing, and poor yet observable trading. Forecast uncertainty is much wider than uncertainty about the historical evidence.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV6, MOAT4, REV8, DUR5, CAP4, CASH2, BAL3, EXEC5 and EARN5. Investment factors are R3, D2, P4 and L1. BQS is 4.78. Raw Growth Quality is 5.75, capped at 5.00 because persistent CASH2 reflects several years of negative conversion. IAS is 0.25×4.78 + 0.35×3 + 0.20×2 + 0.10×4 + 0.10×1 = 3.145. No missing factor is silently assigned a neutral value or reweighted. Every factor has a source-linked rationale in the audit object. The return factor comes from the annual financed model, not a terminal EPS shortcut. A genuine critical reliability failure would make IAS not scoreable; that is not inferred from corrected presentation errors alone. Scoring correction, 20 October 2026: REV is capped at 8 because its historical evidence confidence remains Medium. This reduces BQS from 4.90 to 4.78 and IAS from 3.175 to 3.145; raw GQS falls from 6.15 to 5.75, with final GQS unchanged at 5.00. The weak setup / value-trap risk classification and conditional ranking eligibility are unchanged. No financial model, historical data or issuer information changed.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company fabricates and installs aluminium windows and glass façades for construction projects. It must coordinate design, fabrication, procurement and site installation, then collect milestone invoices and retention after contractual conditions are met. FY26 disclosed façade/window revenue was approximately ₹136.99 crore, with tolling ₹1.5728 crore; tolling includes service, goods and other operating components and is not a separate large earnings engine yet. During FY26 a Hindalco toll agreement was entered for job work. The new Clean-Tech subsidiary and August SolarScape building-integrated-photovoltaic partnership extend the addressable offering, but no separately verified solar growth is added to the model. Orders are execution obligations, not cash equivalents.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Qualification history, fabrication competence and client references create switching friction during a particular project, but do not prove recurring monopoly economics across new bids. The IPO prospectus disclosed an Eternia anchor-partner agreement for the MMRDA region expiring in December 2026, renewable by mutual agreement. FY26's newer tolling arrangement does not itself establish renewal of that original territorial/commercial scope. Projects using Eternia products represented 51.74% of FY23 revenue and 52.22% in the September 2023 half-year; these are dated exposure indicators, not asserted current percentages. Top ten customers represented 67.11% and 59.09% respectively. A contract could last six months to three years, concentrating collection and margin risk. Raw-material procurement, subcontractors and construction schedules limit pricing power. A current renewal or diversified order mix would improve durability, but neither is presumed.

Innovators Facade Systems is a closer operating comparator than an aluminium producer or solar-module company: its primary FY26 report describes the same façade/fenestration execution chain and a larger fabrication footprint. Its FY26 consolidated CFO was ₹37.8377 crore versus ₹3.1364 crore the previous year, but the cash bridge includes ₹34.6757 crore additional trade payables and ₹43.2215 crore other current liabilities. That is a warning against treating one strong peer cash year as permanent economics. Aluwind must demonstrate its own contract collections and funding cycle. No peer trading multiple is imported into the valuation.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Operating revenue for FY21–FY26 was ₹21.2835, ₹28.9865, ₹48.8672, ₹83.4271, ₹109.2248 and ₹138.5649 crore. The five-year CAGR is approximately 45.45%; FY26 growth moderated to 26.86%. The series uses prospectus restated figures and annual-report comparatives, not an undated screening CSV. FY26 has a tiny new subsidiary, so exact parent/group scope is retained rather than implying a six-year consolidated perimeter. PAT over those years was ₹0.7692, ₹0.7880, ₹2.7005, ₹7.5446, ₹8.1214 and ₹10.4455 crore. Profit grew from a low base and is not a stable growth-rate promise. Management's May release cited an approximately ₹300 crore order book and ₹200 crore FY27 turnover objective. The July Cowtown order of ₹12.5946 crore is not simply added to that old backlog without subtracting intervening execution. The base scenario uses ₹180 crore FY27 revenue, below the target; the bull starts at ₹200 crore.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The July 22 proposal envisages about 40,000 square feet of added facility and capacity described as 50 unitized panels per day, versus existing capacity of 20 panels per day operating close to full use. It targets Q1 FY28 and approximately ₹20 crore investment, funded through banks or financial institutions. This is a proposal, not proof of a sanctioned or undrawn loan. More fabrication capacity cannot cure slow customer collections. FY26 inventory, receivables and unbilled revenue total ₹129.363 crore, approximately 93.4% of annual sales. Retention alone is ₹13.6767 crore. An operating-capital proxy including restricted collateral implies roughly 12.5% FY26 NOPAT return on average capital and about 7.2% incremental return. These are analyst calculations, not audited ROIC, and are sensitive to tax normalization and asset classification. The model therefore funds both machinery and working capital rather than assigning growth without reinvestment.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The financial-statement and internal-financial-control opinions reviewed are unmodified. The audit-trail paragraph says the feature operated throughout the year for relevant transactions and no tampering was encountered in test checks; this is not independent verification of every transaction. Related-party disclosures include ₹48 lakh, ₹36 lakh and ₹24 lakh remuneration to the three named Kabra directors, ₹11.11 lakh and ₹13.49 lakh salaries to directors' sons, and ₹6 lakh subsidiary director remuneration. These costs and family involvement warrant scrutiny without automatically establishing abuse. Rajesh Kabra's loan repayment was ₹16.47 lakh with ₹1.01 lakh interest. CFO Varsha Shah's July 31 departure was followed by Aarti Ahuja effectiveAugust 1, so an unresolved-successor claim is stale. The July auditor appointment is for internal audit, not evidence of a statutory auditor walking away. A September independent-director departure was followed by Kailash Goyal's September 28 appointment. The secretary transition and repeated staffing changes remain monitoring matters, not a blanket integrity failure.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY24–26 CFO was −₹2.4053, −₹18.8493 and −₹16.3335 crore, against cumulative PAT ₹26.1115 crore. Cumulative CFO of −₹37.5881 crore means approximately −144% conversion. FY26 stock absorbed ₹27.0187 crore and receivables/unbilled revenue ₹16.1299 crore; higher trade payables supplied ₹14.3594 crore, insufficient to offset that absorption. FY26 capex of ₹4.4689 crore adds to the operating cash deficit. This can reflect growth and contractual timing, but creates real dependence on lenders and equity.

March headline cash of ₹3.2764 crore includes ₹2.9871 crore lien deposits. Another ₹9.6578 crore of lien deposits sits in noncurrent investments, so total restricted collateral is ₹12.6449 crore and free cash is ₹0.2893 crore. Other noncurrent investments comprise property ₹2.0951 crore and physical gold ₹1.7219 crore, not a liquid mutual-fund portfolio. None is freely netted against debt in the base case. Debt rose from ₹13.0946 crore to ₹41.3195 crore. Net current income-tax provision of ₹0.7883 crore is settled once in the model; ordinary government balances remain in working capital.

Two apparent contradictions can be narrowed. FY26's comparative attributable-PAT row repeats prior PBT, but the main PAT line, EPS and original FY25 statements agree on ₹8.1214 crore. Original FY25 CFO of −₹18.3209 crore became −₹18.8493 crore: the exact ₹0.5284 crore change matches reversal of a +₹0.2642 crore investment-gain adjustment to −₹0.2642 crore, offset in investing cash flow without changing total cash. These are specific presentation/classification issues, not evidence that all profit is fictitious. Income-tax disputes of ₹1.0366 crore and GST of ₹0.1582 crore are disclosed; the GST 10% predeposit is recognized in the adverse-settlement sensitivity. A ₹0.1565 crore customer cheque-bounce case is distinct from a company tax obligation. No unassessed arbitrary penalty is inserted into the base.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The linked model has annual FY27–FY31 schedules and a final FY32 April–October stub ending 19 October 2031. The full FY27 schedule bridges from the dated March balance sheet, including unobserved pre-entry movements; it does not claim current October cash is known. Base revenue is ₹180/220/253/278.3/300/318 crore on an annual-rate basis, with EBITDA margins 12/12.5/13/13/13/13%. Operating working capital transitions over two years toward 59% of annual sales, while collateral is 8.5%. Expansion spend is ₹20 crore over the first two years, maintenance 1.5% of sales, and cash interest 11.5% on opening debt plus half-year new borrowing, solved iteratively. Tax is 25% of positive pre-impairment profit. A minimum₹1 crore cash reserve is unavailable for distribution.

The analytical debt ceiling is the lower of ₹80 crore and 3 times annual EBITDA in the base case; it is not a bank covenant or approved line. Gaps require hypothetical equity at 30% below the dated price with 5% issue costs. Base gross equity is₹19.71 crore, new borrowing₹38.68 crore, and shares increase from 2.484742 crore to about 3.10149 crore. Terminal normalized depreciation retains old-asset replacement, expansion depreciation and maintenance economics, rather than valuing fully depreciated equipment as costless. Exit operating-NOPAT multiples are 9/12/15 for bear/base/bull,7 severe: analyst scenarios, not copied peer quotations.

Base terminal value₹72.44 gives 9.68% annual return; bear₹9.98 gives−26.22%; bull₹237.99 gives 39.13%; severe is zero. Working capital 65% reduces base return to 5.97%, interest 13.5% to 8.53%, expansion₹30 crore to 6.76%, and an 11% margin to 0.30%. Realization of property/gold at carrying cost raises return only to 10.59%. These sensitivities show that current low-looking P/E does not compensate automatically for cash and funding needs. No dividends are assumed, no lien deposits are released at exit and no unreceived fundraising proceeds are treated as cash.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Collection delays raise receivables and unbilled work while aluminium, wages and subcontractors still require payment. Lenders may demand more collateral, making reported cash less available. Expansion can consume capital before incremental orders become certified invoices. A partner-contract setback or customer concentration can reduce both margin and credit availability. Bear assumptions use slower revenue,10% EBITDA margin,72% working capital and₹25 crore expansion, requiring₹52.37 crore hypothetical equity. Severe assumptions allow₹12 crore asset impairment and zero residual equity value. Impairments reduce opening recoverable working capital, pass through PAT and are added back as noncash in CFO; replacement funding then occurs once through the working-capital bridge. They are not a second immediate cash payment. If assumed financing is unavailable, operating failure can occur before the modeled terminal date.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold price appreciation in five years needs about 37.97% annual return; tenfold requires 58.49%. The bull scenario reaches₹237.99, about 5.21 times the ₹45.65 entry, but only by growing annual revenue to₹493.35 crore, reaching 15% EBITDA margin, reducing working-capital intensity to 48%, adding capacity on budget and funding₹56.82 crore new debt without equity dilution. That combination is plausible as an upside stress, not the base expectation. Tenfold is outside the modeled outcomes and would require more revenue, better margins, a higher multiple or less financing friction. The same model shows severe loss, so upside arithmetic is not a probability estimate.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: First inspect the next cash-flow and balance-sheet release: cash conversion, inventory ageing, retention collection, unbilled certification, supplier funding and lien deposits matter more than another order headline. Verify actual expansion expenditure, sanctioned funding terms and Q1 FY28 commissioning. Obtain the specific December 2026 Eternia agreement renewal or replacement terms and distinguish them from the newer tolling arrangement. Track CFO/secretary continuity, independent-director approvals, family remuneration and resolution of the disclosed tax/customer cases. Compare any new backlog with execution and cancellations rather than accumulating announcements. For trading, check current lot, spread, depth, order-book availability and exchange restrictions before any implementation; historical turnover is not a fill guarantee.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Funding-sensitive growth watchlist, not a demonstrated cash compounder. BQS4.78, capped Growth Quality 5.00 and conditional IAS3.145 indicate that strong historical sales growth does not offset weak cash conversion and liquidity. Dated trading evidence shows 18 of 20 and 53 of 60 sessions with a security row. Conditional treatment of absent rows as zero reported turnover gives 20-session mean₹9.2284 lakh and median₹3.1526 lakh;60-session median₹3.7215 lakh. A₹5 lakh exit at 5% participation takes 31.72 days using the slower median, before spread or market impact. Latest activity was one 1500-share trade, with one lot costing₹68,475. REG1 flags fewer than 100 unique PANs and generic irregular SME trading, effectiveOctober 21. No active ESM/ASM/GSM code is inferred, and inactive categories do not mean universal clearance. L1 is supported even without pretending a live order book is known.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The annual-report notes, original prior-year statements, IPO prospectus, subsequent primary announcements and dated NSE files are the evidence base. Calculations and analyst assumptions are separated from issuer disclosures. Material unresolved matters are current unrestricted cash and collections; the original Eternia agreement's renewal scope; actual sanctioned expansion funding; future working-capital efficiency; realizability of property/gold; and live execution depth. The forecast explicitly bounds financing and operating outcomes rather than treating these facts as resolved. Historical disclosure errors have precise reconciliations and are not extrapolated into misconduct allegations. This research is not an instruction to execute an investment.

valuation.status: Conditional annual financed model; analyst assumptions, not sanctioned funding
assumption_basis: FY27 base sales of ₹180 crore are below the ₹200 crore management target. Subsequent annual sales are ₹220, ₹253, ₹278.3, ₹300 and ₹318 crore. No separate unverified solar sales are added.
Base EBITDA margin rises from 12% to 13%, close to but above FY26 core operating EBITDA margin of approximately 11.83%. Bear 10% and bull 15% test execution and pricing outcomes.

Opening economic working capital is ₹85.593 crore, including receivables, retention, unbilled work, supplier/employee advances, operating government balances and security deposits, net of ordinary creditors and provisions. It transitions over two years to 59% of revenue in the base case, versus approximately 61.77% initially. Income tax provision is already net and settled separately once.

Only ₹0.2893 crore of March cash is unrestricted. Current and noncurrent lien deposits total ₹12.6449 crore and remain outside distributable cash; additional collateral is funded at 8.5% of revenue in the base case. Property/gold assets of ₹3.817 crore are excluded from base value and tested separately at carrying cost.

Expansion costs ₹20 crore in the base case, split 70%/30% over FY27/FY28, following the disclosed Q1 FY28 target. Maintenance capex is 1.5% of sales, 2% in the bull case. Depreciation uses existing annual ₹1.7459 crore and a ten-year blended life with half-year convention for additions; terminal replacement depreciation is normalized rather than eliminated when book assets age. These blended lives and maintenance spending are analyst estimates, not a verified engineering bill.

Interest is 11.5% on opening debt and half-year new borrowing, solved iteratively. Disclosed bank/NBFC rates span 8.15–13.50%, supporting a range rather than an artificially low historical blended expense. The base debt ceiling is the lower of ₹80 crore and three times annual EBITDA; this is an analytical limit, not approved credit. Residual funding requires equity at a 30% price discount and 5% issuance fee. No-financing failure can be worse than the funded scenarios.

Tax is 25% of positive pre-impairment profit; no impairment tax shield is assumed. Loss stresses reduce opening recoverable working capital, charge PAT and add back the noncash amount before funding closing working capital once. A separate tax-dispute sensitivity charges ₹1.0366 crore income tax plus 90% of the ₹0.1582 crore GST amount after the disclosed predeposit; this is not an expected base liability.

Opening shares of 2.484742 crore agree with reported shares and the dated security master. Model equity issuance explicitly increases the denominator. No unreceived fundraising or automatic restricted-deposit release is included.

Exit operating-NOPAT multiples are 9, 12 and 15 times, 7 in the severe case, as analyst scenarios. No dividend is assumed. Five full fiscal-year forecasts and an exact final April–October stub end five years after the dated entry.
